options: A secret key for your app
A message you send to the AI
A saved snapshot of your project — a save point you can return to

explain.right: Each commit records the state of your files at that moment, so you have a history and can roll back.
explain.wrong: It's not a chat message, a live site, or a secret — it's a local save point in your project's history.

items.q: What does GitHub add on top of git?
options: It is the programming language your app uses
It makes your app run faster
It writes your code for you
An online, hosted copy of your repository — backup, a shareable link, and collaboration

explain.right: GitHub hosts a remote copy of your repo so it's backed up, shareable by link, and reachable by others.
explain.wrong: It doesn't write code, isn't a language, and doesn't change your app's speed — it's where the repo lives online.

items.q: Where does an API key belong?
options: In the README so you don't forget it
In an ignored file (like .env) read at runtime — never committed to the repo
Pushed to GitHub so it's safely backed up

explain.right: Secrets live in a gitignored file and are read from the environment; the repo holds code, never the secret value.
explain.wrong: Hard-coding, putting it in the README, or pushing it to GitHub all expose the key to anyone who can see the repo.

items.q: You accidentally committed an API key and pushed it to GitHub. What's the real fix?
options: Nothing, it's fine once it's pushed
Revoke/rotate the key so the old one stops working, then issue a new one — because git history keeps the old commit
Just delete the line in a new commit — that removes it
Make the repo private and keep using the same key

explain.right: Git history still contains the key even after you delete the line, so you must invalidate it and replace it.
explain.wrong: Deleting the line, doing nothing, or going private all leave the leaked key usable in history — rotate it.

items.q: Describe the deploy path: how does code on your machine become a public website, and who performs the final deploy click?
rubric: Code is pushed to GitHub (version control)
A hosting platform connects to the repo, builds/runs the app, and gives a public URL
Secrets are set on the host (env vars), not in the repo
The human performs the final deploy/authorize click — dronAIcharya preps up to that point

explain.right: Strong answers trace code → GitHub → host builds from the repo → public URL, with secrets on the host and the final click left to the human.
explain.wrong: A weak answer says 'the AI just puts it online' or forgets that the account-linked deploy step is the user's.
